unsupported_claims: Evidence of hurt performance would show scores flat or declining beyond 8 workers while wall-clock time keeps improving (goes along with the false premise as a hypothetical expectation)

Such results usually stem from asynchronous SGD races and reduced effective learning-rate or sampling quality (contradicts the paper's claim that sparse updates make ASGD near-optimal and lose no performance)
rationale: The answer never corrects the false premise; the source says parallelization gives consistent speedup and no loss of predictive performance up to 8 workers. It instead speculates about how such degradation would appear and its causes, which the paper does not support, though it does hedge by saying it cannot identify the study.
